Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
255 PM EDT Tue May 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Nothing.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Gusty thunderstorms are possible Wednesday afternoon and 
evening.

2) After another cool down, above average temperatures return 
for the weekend into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Gusty thunderstorms are possible Wednesday 
afternoon and evening.

UL trof progged to move across GL with corresponding SFC low
moving east Wed. WAA will prevail ahead of FROPA with gusty s'ly
winds. This will bring temps into the 70s areawide. Initial wave
may bring some showers, but LL dry air in place likely limits
ern extent. Second round of convection could be more robust
given the background shear. There may be some storm
organization. Given timing of tstorms near Alleghenies around
peak heating, SPC has MRGL (Level 1 out of 5) for SVR WX on Wed.
Storms should gradually weaken as they move east. Some models do
have a few tenths of QPF west of I-95 as storms diminish. The 
main threat will be strong to locally damaging winds.

KEY MESSAGE 2...After another cool down, above average 
temperatures return for the weekend into early next week.

Cooler Thu with ULL over NE. Some residual upslope rain showers
during the day, with low probs of a shower E of the mtns. 

High pres builds overhead Fri which marks the start of the warm
up. UL ridging continues to build in through the weekend. Highs
by Sat & Sun likely widespread 80s (outside terrain) with low
SW may bring shower and tstorm potential at some point between 
Sat and Sun, but low confidence. Drier air moves into the 
region at the start of next week as upper level ridging builds, 
minimizing additional rain chances.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected with light and variable winds 
becoming S/SE in the afternoon. Some gustiness may develop 
overnight at times, with gusts to 25 kt more common on 
Wed. There may be multiple rounds of showers and embedded 
tstorms, one during midday to afternoon, and the second during 
the evening. Any tstorms could contain gusty outflow, 
especially at MRB. The cold front tracks through Wed night, 
which brings an end to any showers and shifts winds to the 
NW. 

An ULL will be nearby on Thu into Fri which will likely add 
stratocumulus, with a worst case being MVFR ceilings at times. 
NW'ly winds will also gust to 25 kt.

A SW potentially brings some scattered showers in the Sat 
afternoon/evening timeframe, but prevailing VFR conditions are 
otherwise expected otherwise. Light winds Fri night shift 
SW Sat afternoon.

&&

.MARINE...
S'ly flow will take hold this afternoon, increasing tonight as 
high pressure departs. Gusts of 20 to 25 knots will be 
commonplace across a majority of the waters, especially by 
Wed. While wind gust forecasts are tricky on the interior 
waterways during the overnight, have eventually all waters 
entering a SCA tonight. The current advisory continues through 
6 PM WEd, although it will likely need to be extended into the 
evening. Some late afternoon to evening tstorms. could impact 
the waters as the cold front approaches from the west. Any 
stronger storm may require SMWs.

Winds shift to W-NW early Thu behind the cold front. Winds will
increase through the day, and advisories will likely be needed.
SCA conditions likely continue through Fri afternoon. Winds 
fall below SCA criteria by Fri evening. NW winds shift 
S'ly by the afternoon on Sat.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Expect a gradual uptick in water levels ahead of a mid-week 
low pressure system. The influence of increasing s'lies will 
carry the tidal forecast to action stage at several locations 
during times of high tide. The Stevens ensemble shows the 
potential for Minor tidal flooding by early Thu at Annapolis. 
Expect anomalies to fall thereafter as winds shift to NW'ly.

&&
